Adds family-specific exhaustive validators, including independent size component checks and opacity validation for negative, finite-above-one, non-finite, and accepted zero and one values.
Covers all five public scalar seams, complete vocabulary traversal, diagnostics, unchanged resolution, and opacity range boundaries including finite 1.25.
Demonstrates realistic semantic usage of all five scalar families through the shared app-owned aggregate design system.

Records this run's implementation evidence, approved Makefile scope amendment, validation outcome, and one-to-one connected-change bookkeeping.

commands_run: Safe validation profile test: passed through make:test with 17 Swift Testing tests.

Safe validation profile all: attempted through the repository validator; it returned VALIDATION_PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE before selecting or executing a command, so make all was not run and no validation artifact was produced for this attempt.

Verified product-spec and product-contract SHA-256 values match the run baseline.
tests: Passed: all 17 Swift Testing tests, including existing spacing and semantic-color coverage.
Passed: scalar resolver tests preserve valid, negative, out-of-range, infinite, and NaN values.
Passed: validator tests enumerate complete vocabularies, report multiple issues, and continue; size width and height are checked independently.
Passed: opacity validation accepts 0 and 1, reports negative opacity and finite 1.25, reports non-finite values, and leaves resolver values unchanged.
Not run: safe all profile; the validation runner rejected it before selecting a command.

product_acceptance_criteria.evidence: Each family has its own marker and independent capability protocol; tests use single-family conformers and a non-Hashable, non-RawRepresentable token type.
Dimension, corner radius, and stroke width return CGFloat; size returns CGSize; opacity returns Double through direct synchronous protocol requirements.
Resolver tests assert finite, negative, out-of-range, infinite, and NaN values unchanged; opacity values are checked again after validation.
Five capability-specific validators iterate their associated token type's allCases and report violations without changing resolver behavior.
The shared ExampleDesignSystem conforms to all five new capabilities and consumes each through frame, rounded shape, stroke, and opacity SwiftUI modifiers.
New token, capability, resolver, and validator DocC states logical-point or normalized unitless opacity semantics, validation policy, and the absence of production repair.

technical_acceptance_criteria.evidence: DimensionToken, SizeToken, CornerRadiusToken, StrokeWidthToken, and OpacityToken require only Sendable and CaseIterable.
Five independent Sendable protocols expose direct resolvers with the specified CGFloat, CGSize, and Double return types.
scalarResolversReturnAppAuthoredValuesUnchanged covers valid, negative, out-of-range, infinite, and NaN values for all five families.
DesignSystemTestSupport exports validateDimensions, validateSizes, validateCornerRadii, validateStrokeWidths, and validateOpacities; each loops over allCases.
Per-family tests compare observed resolution history with the full vocabulary and capture all expected invalid-token diagnostics; a valid vocabulary produces no issues.
Size validation independently checks width and height for finiteness and negativity; opacity accepts 0 and 1 and reports negative, finite-above-one (1.25), and non-finite values.
The one immutable shared example aggregate maps app-owned tokens and uses every family in SwiftUI construction; Serena reported no Swift diagnostics for the example.

Every new public token, capability, resolver, and TestSupport validator has DocC describing semantics, units or native type, test expectations, and no production sanitization; capability resolution is documented as synchronous and nonthrowing.
The safe test profile passed all 17 tests, including existing spacing, semantic-color, and package-import tests; Package.swift and the two product-definition files were left unchanged.

blockers: The requested repository-safe validation profile all returned VALIDATION_PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE before command selection. The Makefile all target delegates to test, but the validator did not expose that target; the required make all validation evidence is therefore unavailable.
